title: Egyptian FM Abdelatty Discusses Iran Nuclear Negotiations with US Envoy Witkoff
detail: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held a call with US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff to discuss the latest developments in US-Iran nuclear negotiations. Egypt, which played a behind-the-scenes facilitation role in the February-March 2026 US-Iran ceasefire, is closely monitoring the nuclear talks given their implications for regional stability and Egypt's mediation leverage. As a non-nuclear-weapons state that borders both the Gaza conflict zone and the Red Sea, Egypt has a direct stake in any framework that constrains Iranian military capacity. The call reflects Egypt's continued effort to position itself as an indispensable diplomatic interlocutor between the US and the broader Middle East.

media.caption: Egypt's FM Abdelatty speaks with US envoy Witkoff on Iran nuclear negotiations

title: Egypt-Sudan War Regionalization Deepens; Analysts Warn of SAF 'Alibi War' Framing
detail: Horn Review published an analysis arguing the Sudan Armed Forces (SAF) — backed by Egypt — are increasingly using the 'internationalization' and 'regionalization' framing of the conflict (Egypt vs. UAE/RSF, Ethiopia proxy dynamics) to justify continued fighting and deflect accountability for civilian harm. The analysis, titled 'The SAF's Alibi War,' noted that Egypt-Sudan-Ethiopia triangular tensions, the closure of Egypt's Pagak base by South Sudan, and reported Egyptian officer casualties in combat are being weaponized narratively by SAF to maintain domestic and regional support. Egypt's Uganda Nile cooperation pledge (made by FM Abdelatty to Ugandan counterpart) was seen as a diplomatic move to shore up downstream Nile Basin allies as the GERD dispute remains unresolved.

media.caption: Analysis warns Egypt-Sudan-Ethiopia proxy dynamics are being used by SAF as a narrative 'alibi' for continued war
